[PATH:empirical] Controlled scaling experiments on transformer-based language models measuring performance on out-of-distribution reasoning tasks (e.g., ARC, GSM8K) across multiple orders of magnitude of compute — If performance on such tasks plateaus or shows diminishing returns beyond a certain scale, it would support the hypothesis that scaling alone is insufficient. Conversely, continued log-linear improvement would refute it.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of transformer expressivity in terms of circuit complexity and algorithmic reasoning (e.g., bounds on solving parity, composition, or hierarchical tasks) — Proving or disproving that transformers cannot efficiently represent certain classes of functions (e.g., those requiring recursion or global state tracking) would provide a formal basis for the claimed inherent limitations.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of recent literature on emergent abilities and scaling failures in large models (e.g., papers from NeurIPS, ICLR, or arXiv surveys on scaling laws and capability saturation) — Aggregating empirical and theoretical findings from the community can reveal whether consistent patterns of scaling failure exist across architectures and tasks, helping to confirm or refute the necessity of fundamental breakthroughs.
